Why does my retry wrapper double the request rate after a timeout?

Asked 2 days agoViewed 182 times3 answers

I wrote a small retry wrapper around an HTTP client. When a request times out after thirty seconds, the wrapper starts a new attempt immediately, but the original request is still running in the background.

The result is that a single logical request becomes two or three concurrent requests, and our rate limiter starts rejecting everything for the next minute.

Report · Edit

Accepted answer

42 votesUpvote

A timeout on the client side does not cancel the underlying request. Unless you explicitly abort it, the socket stays open and the server keeps working.

Pass a cancellation token from your wrapper into the HTTP call, and abort it when the timeout fires. In most clients the abort closes the connection and releases the slot.

ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(parent, 30*time.Second)
defer cancel()

Other answers

11 votesUpvote

Worth adding that retries should also use a deadline budget, not just a per-attempt timeout, or a slow dependency can hold a worker far longer than you expect.

6 votesUpvote

If the server supports idempotency keys, send one per logical request. Then a retried request that reaches the server twice is safe to deduplicate instead of doubling the load.
